newsitem.title: CHINA: China jails businessman for financial swindle.
newsitem.headline: China jails businessman for financial swindle.

text.p: A court in China's northeastern Heilongjiang province has sentenced a businessman to life inprisonment for embezzling loans worth more than 284 million yuan ($34.2 million), court officials said on Tuesday.
Harbin People's Intermediate Court sentenced Liu Jinbiao, chairman of a real estate company in the provincial capital Harbin, at a hearing late last month, a court official said.
Liu, 58, had lodged an appeal, but the court had yet to decide when to hear it, the official told Reuters by telephone.

Between June 1994 and April 1995, Liu had embezzled 284.11 million yuan in loans from a provincial investment bank and the Harbin-based department of a securities company by bribing officials and faking contracts, he said.
Liu had used a state-owned stadium project as a pretext for acquiring the loans, leaving the proposed stadium hundreds of millions of yuan short of the investment it needed, he said.
Besides 93.45 million yuan used for paying debts and more than 56 million yuan seized by judicial officials, Liu had squandered the rest of the loans, he said, but give no details.
Liu had been sentenced to eight years imprisonment for other crimes in 1972, the Worker's Daily said, but did not elaborate.
